summary: This benchmark rigorously evaluates when adding an opposite-translated third camera aids or harms depth estimation on occluded surfaces using a controlled synthetic multi-view patch-matching testbed. While the additional view substantially boosts depth recovery on newly visible pixels (36.7% to 92.6%), naive error minimization and round-trip consistency routing both cause net accuracy degradations across the overall foreground. The work is exceptionally well-controlled and mathematically consistent, though constrained by a synthetic discrete-depth setup without global regularization.
strengths: Carefully controlled benchmark design incorporating negative controls (mismatched view, duplicate view, matched-budget random routing).
Reports complete contingency counts, exact ratios, and 95% paired bootstrap confidence intervals.
Provides a counterintuitive and valuable negative result demonstrating that standard round-trip consistency gating fails to improve overall accuracy over baseline.
Concise and mathematically consistent reporting of experimental data across multiple independent panels.
weaknesses: Evaluation relies strictly on a simplified synthetic renderer with discrete depth candidates and unregularized 3x3 local patch matching rather than modern continuous or regularized multi-view stereo pipelines.
Lacks qualitative error analysis or visual diagrams illustrating the specific geometric configurations where round-trip routing introduced false positives.
Submitted under text_only status without an attached code repository bundle in the submission metadata, relying only on inline commit links.
suggestions: Test whether incorporating semi-global matching (SGM) or smoothness priors prevents the foreground accuracy degradation observed with naive min-pooling.
Include sample visual disparity maps illustrating typical failure modes of the round-trip consistency router.
Formally package the benchmark harness and synthetic rendering pipeline into the submission repository bundle to enable verified open badge status.

claims.text: An opposite-side camera raised exact depth accuracy from 36.7% to 92.6% on synthetic pixels hidden from the first translated view and visible to the second.
claims.source: Internal mathematical verification from reported counts: 2,252 / 6,135 = 36.71% and 5,680 / 6,135 = 92.58%

claims.text: On an independent panel with a smaller camera displacement the gain was 49.4% to 82.2%.
claims.source: Internal mathematical verification from reported counts: 719 / 1,456 = 49.38% and 1,197 / 1,456 = 82.21%

novelty_vs_existing.title: End-to-End Learning of Geometry and Context for Deep Stereo Regression
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: While Kendall et al. train deep regularized 3D cost volumes for binocular stereo, this submission isolates the unlearned geometric utility and occlusion trade-offs of opposite-view third cameras under pure local patch matching.
